h1: Postpartum Hair Loss: When It Stops and What Helps
subtitle: The shedding that starts around month three. It is real, and it does end.

hero.alt: 200x close-up of the scalp during postpartum shedding, with many short regrowing hairs among the openings
hero.caption: The shed and the regrowth, side by side, at 200x.

quickAnswer: During pregnancy, higher estrogen keeps more hairs than usual in their growth phase, so shedding slows and hair feels thicker. After birth, estrogen drops and all of those held hairs move into shedding together. That is why the loss typically begins around two to four months postpartum and can feel alarming. For most people it settles within six to twelve months, and the hairline regrows a fringe of short new hairs on the way back. What can keep it going longer is low iron, thyroid changes after birth, breastfeeding demands, or very little sleep. Those are checkable. We read your scalp at 200x at Nina Ross Atlanta in Sandy Springs and look at the systems behind it. Serving all of Metro Atlanta.
takeaways: It usually starts two to four months after birth.
Most people see it settle within six to twelve months.
If it runs longer, iron and thyroid are worth checking.

items.you: Handfuls come out in the shower
items.why: After birth, the hairs pregnancy held in growth shift into shedding together. It feels like a lot because it is, and it is commonly temporary.
items.check: We confirm the pattern at 200x and check whether new growth has already started along your hairline.

items.you: It started a few months after I gave birth
items.us: Delayed onset, two to four months postpartum
items.why: The shed arrives two to four months after delivery because that is how long the resting phase lasts before hairs release.
items.check: We match the timing to your delivery date, which usually confirms postpartum shedding.

items.you: Short baby hairs all along my hairline
items.us: Regrowth fringe of new anagen hairs
items.why: A band of short new hairs along the hairline is a good sign. It usually means the follicles have already restarted.
items.check: We read the fringe at 200x and photograph it, so you can see regrowth before it is obvious in the mirror.

items.why: Postpartum shedding is diffuse, so the part can look wider while hair is released all over the scalp.
items.check: We compare several areas at 200x to confirm it is diffuse shedding and check for any pattern thinning underneath.

items.you: It has been more than a year
items.why: Shedding past a year is commonly linked to a second driver, such as low iron, a thyroid change or very little sleep.
items.check: We look at iron, thyroid and nutrient status in-house to find what is still keeping it going.

items.title: Estrogen drop after delivery
items.text: The hairs pregnancy held in growth all shift into shedding at once. This is the main driver and it is self-limiting.

items.title: Iron and nutrient depletion
items.text: Pregnancy, blood loss at delivery and breastfeeding all draw down iron stores, and low ferritin keeps shedding going after the hormonal wave passes.

items.title: Postpartum thyroid changes
items.text: Thyroid function shifts after birth for some people. It is easy to test and worth ruling in or out when shedding runs long.

items.title: Sleep and stress load
items.text: Sustained cortisol from broken sleep keeps follicles cycling out early, which stretches the recovery.

insight.kicker: What we see that others miss
insight.title: The regrowth fringe is the signal to look for
paras: At 200x along the hairline we look for a band of short, tapered, fully pigmented hairs, all roughly the same length. That fringe means the follicles have already restarted, even while you are still finding hair in the shower drain.

insight.text: If that fringe is missing after a year, that is when we start looking at iron and thyroid rather than reassuring you.

faq.a: Most people see it settle between six and twelve months after birth. If you are past a year and still shedding heavily, that is worth investigating rather than waiting out.

faq.q: Will my hair come back the same?
faq.a: For most people density returns as the regrowth fringe fills in. If something else is going on, such as low iron or pattern thinning underneath, we tell you. Results not typical. Individual results will vary.

faq.q: Should I take a hair vitamin?
faq.a: Test before another bottle goes in the cart. If your labs show a real gap, we correct that specifically. If they are clean, a vitamin is unlikely to change the timeline.

faq.q: Is it safe to come in while breastfeeding?
faq.a: Yes. The scalp read is non-invasive, and we take breastfeeding into account in anything we recommend.

faq.q: Can I wear braids or a protective style through it?
faq.a: Yes. We look at your scalp and work with the styles that make your life manageable, keeping tension at the hairline in mind while it recovers.
